## On-box observation: both runtime acceptance criteria are satisfied

The change merged as `a516c4a834f` (Gerrit rebased it server-side on submit, so the merged
SHA differs from the pushed revision `bf6e64c0993`; `rebar-ticket: 011f-4424-fcfc-4ce9` is
carried on the merged commit).

**Alarm returned to OK.** `rebar-autodeploy-errors` is `OK` as of 2026-09-20T15:13:37Z, which
is after the merge:

```
Threshold Crossed: 3 out of the last 4 datapoints [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
were not greater than the threshold (0.0)
```

Three consecutive zero-error datapoints, so this is a real recovery rather than an
insufficient-data lapse. No other alarm in this account is in ALARM except
`rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high`, which has been stale since 2026-09-09 and is unrelated.

**The stranded container was reaped, and the sweep is now correct.** `docker ps -a` on
`i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (`rebar-gerrit`) shows exactly one MCP container:

```
rebar-mcp-a516c4a834f7-8093    Up 11 minutes (healthy)
```

The stranded `rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092` this ticket was filed against is **gone**. Note
what the surviving name proves beyond the reap: its SHA suffix is `a516c4a834f7`, the very
commit that carries this fix, so autodeploy picked up the merge, started a backend from it,
retired the stale one, and left the host with a single healthy binding on a fresh port — the
end state this ticket specifies, observed rather than inferred.
